calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Affected areas and owners:
- pharmacy-ops: Dispensing, controlled substances (DEA), pharmacist scope, vaccines → Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations)
- drug-safety: OTC products, labeling, recalls, shortages (FDA) → Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality)
- payers: Medicare Part D, Medicaid and insurer billing (CMS) → Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement)
- privacy-people: Patient privacy (HIPAA), records, store workforce → Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-06, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-06; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I could confirm one document in the 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06 window that plausibly affects CornerCare, and its details are thin. I ran out of searches before I could open each day's full issue, so this list may be incomplete.

## Documents found

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Document number** | 2026-22285 |
| **Title** | Not retrieved. It is a DEA rule, signed by the DEA Federal Register Liaison Officer. It replaces the penalty wording "of not more than $30,000" with "under title 18, United States Code" in the "Affidavit for New Pharmacy" and "Affidavit for Transfer of Pharmacy" text. It was filed 10-30-26 and appears in the November 2, 2026 issue. |
| **URL** | https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22285 (short link built from the document number, not seen in search results) |
| **Key deadline** | Effective date not retrieved. |
| **Tier** | **High (provisional).** It is a final rule. It becomes Critical if it took effect between 2026-10-07 and 2026-11-06, which is likely if it was effective on publication. I couldn't confirm that. |
| **Owner** | pharmacy-ops (Priya Raman) |
| **Reason** | It changes the penalty language in the DEA affidavits pharmacies sign when opening or transferring a pharmacy. |
| **Action** | Pull the full text and effective date. Update the affidavit templates used for new-store and pharmacy-transfer DEA filings. |

## Lead I couldn't fully verify

- **DEA technical amendment to 21 CFR 1301.16(b)** (Docket DEA-1303, RIN 1117-ZA09), published in the November 4 issue. It adds "or registrant" so the rule on amending or withdrawing registration applications covers renewals as well as new applications. DEA says it adds no new or substantive requirements for registrants. I didn't retrieve its document number or URL, so I've left it out of the table. If you confirm it, it would be a final rule owned by pharmacy-ops. It would likely rate Critical if effective on publication, otherwise High. The action is low effort: tell whoever handles DEA renewals.

## Reviewed and excluded

- **2026-22739** (published Nov 6): the CY 2027 hospital outpatient (OPPS) and ambulatory surgical center payment final rule. It covers hospital payment, so it does not apply.
- **2026-22663** (Nov 6): an FDA technical amendment to food additive petition addresses. It is about animal food, so it does not apply.
- **2026-22427 and 2026-22369** (Nov 3): FDA guidance on cellular and gene therapy potency and on hepatitis B blood-donation testing. Neither applies to a pharmacy.
- **2026-22553, 22555 and 22556** (Nov 5): DEA importer and manufacturer registration notices. These are manufacturer-only matters.
- **2026-22380** (Nov 3): an HHS final rule on disability nondiscrimination in federally funded programs. I only saw the title, so I can't say whether it reaches pharmacies. It may be worth a quick check by Sam Whitaker.
- **Outside the window:**
  - The Medicare Drug Price Negotiation and Part D final rule (2026-22792). CMS announced it on November 5, but the Federal Register scheduled publication for November 9.
  - The DEA production quota documents (2026-22842 and 2026-22843), published November 10.
  - The HIPAA Privacy Rule final rule (2026-23429), published November 19.
